annotation.title_clean: Design of Robotic Care: Ethical Implications of a Multi-Actor Perspective
annotation.title_en: Design of Robotic Care: Ethical Implications of a Multi-Actor Perspective
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Caic, M.; Holmlid, S.; Mahr, D.; Odekerken-Schröder, G.
annotation.venue: Service Design Practices for Healthcare Innovation (Springer)
annotation.summary_en: Book chapter reporting an interview study of 36 older adults, informal and formal caregivers on the ethical and social implications of robotic elderly care. Three thematic maps (assistance, monitoring, companionship) show perceived well-being benefits alongside fears of reduced agency, privacy loss and delusion, and caregivers' reluctance to accept robots as co-providers.
key_provisions_or_claims: Interviewed 36 actors using generative phenomenographic interviews and visualizations of future care networks
Three thematic maps: assistance, monitoring, companionship
Social robots may improve well-being through service, constant presence and reliability
Ethical concerns include decline in agency, loss of privacy and delusion
Formal caregivers give desirable answers but resist placing robots close to older persons
